runs.goal_hypothesis: Establish an unshaped 30%-defensive-opening curriculum baseline over 15.36M steps.

results_insights.insight: The curriculum produced limited defensive competence.
The limited defensive-X result occurred over 25.34-move games.
At least one side remained winless.

reasoning: The initial defensive-opening regimen was insufficient for broad competence.
Multiple defining knobs differ from earlier historical regimens, limiting cross-group attribution.
Finite evaluation and training seed variation may affect exact percentages.

runs.goal_hypothesis: Test slight defense-biased shaping and annealed learning rate without defensive openings, relative to 7d72c2dc21f54ccf970746f72505cd49.

results_insights.insight: Aggregate improved by 0.1317 over the opening baseline.
The improved defensive-X evaluation lasted 19.67 moves on average.
Combined-X games lasted longer and reached 33% wins.

reasoning: Shaping plus annealing learned stronger defense despite no installed defensive openings.
Opening probability, shaping, and learning-rate schedule all changed, so causality is confounded.
Stochasticity and side-specific evaluation sampling remain plausible contributors.

runs.goal_hypothesis: Add 30% defensive openings and use a fixed 0.0001 start/final rate with the slight shaped configuration of 0905ff28c6e946828a4698e40a02ebae.

results_insights.insight: Performance fell by 0.0933 relative to the no-opening annealed run.
Games lasted longer despite fewer wins.

reasoning: Adding openings did not offset the less aggressive learning-rate schedule.
Opening probability and starting rate changed together, preventing isolated attribution.
Longer episodes may reflect resistance rather than improved winning competence.

runs.goal_hypothesis: Retry the shaped 30%-opening curriculum with annealed 0.0003-to-0.0001 learning rate, relative to 5d5fd425d4604e88a61c05f8cfd56451.

results_insights.insight: Higher starting rate reduced aggregate performance by 0.0617.
Defensive competence collapsed relative to the fixed-rate predecessor.
Very long games still ended in only 6% wins.

reasoning: Annealing from 0.0003 was harmful in this otherwise matched comparison.
Training stochasticity may contribute because there is only one run per setting.
Episode-length inflation without wins suggests survival alone is not an adequate objective.
